summary: The audit checks two of the three contemporary areas (philosophy of science or logic, moral and political philosophy, contemporary theoretical philosophy) and Philosophy electives numbered 10 and above to reach 30 units, at least 10 of them numbered 100 or above. PHIL 196-199 do not count, letter-graded courses need a C- or better, and at most 10 units graded S or CR count. Checked by hand: a history of philosophy course numbered 100 or above, which you move in, the 3-unit minimum for letter-graded courses, and at most two transfer courses for 10 units. The Bulletin gives the S/CR limit as both ten and six units, so confirm it with the department.

VMez56y5.why: "Complete a History of Philosophy course numbered 100 or above and for a minimum of three units." The Bulletin lists no History of Philosophy courses for the minor, so the student moves one in.

Dv0sn6jK.why: "Any course 10 and above except for 196-199." The electives make up the rest of the minor's 30 units, which the audit counts. Contemporary Philosophy asks for "at least 2 of the following" areas, so a course in a third area still counts toward the 30 units. Every other area course is numbered 10 or above and already falls in this pool; PHIL 2 (Moral and Political Philosophy) does not, and the audit dropped it whenever it chose the other two areas, so it is listed here too.
